summary: The flexible-time PhD program is a registration option that differs from the full-time PhD program only in design and delivery. The flexible-time PhD program option is for practicing professionals in the relevant field of study who require a modified time period and/or content delivery option to complete the requirements of their program.
requirements: Satisfy SGS General Regulations and Degree Regulations in the SGS Calendar, including good academic standing, supervision, and candidacy regulations.
Register full-time for the first 4 years and part-time for subsequent years.
Maintain continuous registration for every session, including summers, unless granted a leave of absence.
Constitute a supervisory committee by the end of the first session in Year 3.
Achieve candidacy by the end of the fourth year of registration.
duration: Program length is normally 5 to 6 years (up to 7 years depending on unit); time limit is between 6 and 8 years.
benefits: Extended program timeline allowing concurrent professional practice while completing a PhD.
Reduced (part-time) fees starting in Year 5 of registration.

Must meet the same admission requirements as applicants to the full-time PhD program under SGS General Regulations and Degree Regulations.
Must demonstrate that proposed research/program of study is related to professional work and vice versa.
Must continue professional activities while registered in the program.
Must apply to a graduate unit approved by University governance to offer the flexible-time PhD option.
Subject to the availability of a supervisor.
howToApply: Submit an application to an approved graduate unit offering the flexible-time PhD program option.
Demonstrate practicing professional status and alignment between professional work and proposed research during the application process.
Secure/confirm availability of a supervisor.

Assessment of applicant's status as a practicing professional and the mutual relevance of research and professional work.

summary: The “Monitoring Guidelines” are intended to be a companion document to the “ Supervision Guidelines ”. The goal of the “Monitoring Guidelines” is to provide general recommendations for graduate units on creating structures and processes to support doctoral student success by ensuring that students can make timely progression through their programs. There is likely to be considerable variance in the implementation of some of the recommended procedures, depending, for example, on the nature of the scholarly discipline and the research environment (including the size of graduate unit), or the degree to which research is conducted independently. Graduate units are encouraged to implement the guidelines in a manner appropriate to their discipline and program as well as communicate the relevant procedures in a clear and transparent manner to graduate students and faculty.
requirements: Select a thesis topic or research area and approve a supervisor as early as possible in the program.
Meet regularly with the supervisor (recommended minimum frequency: weekly, biweekly, or at least once a month depending on field practice).
Meet with the supervisory committee at least annually (or more frequently, such as twice per year) to assess progress.
Participate in progress evaluations and sign supervisory committee reports.
Maintain good academic standing and meet required program/curricular milestones (e.g., coursework, comprehensive exam, achieving candidacy, proposal defense).
documents: Written materials for feedback (e.g., research proposals, manuscripts, grant and funding applications, conference submissions).
Supervisory committee progress reports (including explicit written comments and progress evaluation).
Student written comments or appended responses to supervisory committee reports (optional/as needed).
Research and academic plan (required in cases of remediation following an unsatisfactory progress report).
benefits: Provides structured institutional oversight and continuous supervisory support to ensure timely progression through doctoral programs.

Access to university support services including SGS Financial Aid and Advising, Centre for International Experience (CIE), Accessibility Services, Health and Wellness, Centre for Graduate Mentorship and Supervision (CGMS), Graduate Centre for Academic Communication (GCAC), and Centre for Graduate Professional Development (CGPD).
eligibility: Targeted at doctoral students and graduate units at the University of Toronto.
howToApply: Not stated on source (This document details institutional progress monitoring guidelines for registered doctoral students rather than an application process for funding).
selectionProcess: Supervisory committees conduct annual (or semi-annual) progress evaluations and prepare a committee report detailing observations and recommendations.
Reports provide a clear judgment on student progress linked to degree-level expectations and learning objectives (e.g., satisfactory, unsatisfactory, or probationary).
Reports are reviewed and signed by the student, supervisor, committee members, and the graduate unit representative (graduate chair/coordinator or administrator).
If a student receives an unsatisfactory progress report, a remediation process is initiated (e.g., re-evaluation within three months).

If insufficient academic progress is recorded in two consecutive supervisory committee reports, the graduate chair/coordinator consults the Vice Dean, Students, SGS regarding potential termination of registration.
requiresSupervisor: Supervisors must be chosen from among graduate faculty members of the student's graduate unit with SGS-approved Graduate Faculty Memberships. Supervisors are required to meet regularly with students, identify challenges early, and provide timely written feedback.

summary: At the School of Graduate Studies, posthumous degrees can be awarded to students who pass away before graduation, in circumstances that conform to the official Posthumous Award of Degrees policy (1976), managed by the University of Toronto Governing Council. What follows are the procedures for the award of a PhD degree, and those for Master’s degrees.

eligibility: The deceased student must have been registered in good standing at the time of death or within the preceding 12 months.

For Master's candidates: Must have completed at least 75% of total program credit requirements at the time of death.
howToApply: The Chair or Graduate Coordinator of the student's graduate unit submits a recommendation letter and supporting documents to the SGS Associate Director, Graduate Academic Services.

If appraisals and conditions are met, the graduate unit forwards the recommendation to the Non-Standard Admissions and Programs Committee.
Upon approval by the Non-Standard Admissions and Programs Committee, the recommendation is submitted to the Academic Board of Governing Council.
If approved by the Academic Board, SGS informs the graduate unit, and the Dean of SGS writes a letter to the student's family.
